chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عِيسَى، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

chunks.arabic_text: خَرَجْتُ عَامًا مِنَ الْأَعْوَامِ وَمَعِي مَالٌ كَثِيرٌ لِأَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ، وَأَوْدَعَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ يَقْطِينَ رِسَالَةً سَأَلَهُ الدُّعَاءَ، فَلَمَّا فَرَغْتُ مِنْ حَوَائِجِي وَأَوْصَلْتُ الْمَالَ إِلَيْهِ قُلْتُ: جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ سَأَلَنِي عَلِيُّ بْنُ يَقْطِينَ أَنْ تَدْعُوَ اللَّهَ لَهُ، فَقَالَ: لِلْآخِرَةِ؟ قُلْتُ: نَعَمْ، قَالَ: فَوَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَى صَدْرِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ: ضَمَنْتُ لِعَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينَ أَلَّا تَمِسَّهُ النَّارُ

translations.en: I set out one year with a lot of wealth belonging to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and Ali ibn Yaqtin had entrusted me with a message asking for his supplication. When I finished attending to my duties and delivered the wealth to him, I said: May I be your ransom, Ali ibn Yaqtin asked me to request that you supplicate to Allah for him. He (peace be upon him) asked: For the hereafter? I said: Yes. He placed his hand on his chest and then said: I guarantee for Ali ibn Yaqtin that the fire will not touch him.

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the spiritual status of Ali ibn Yaqtin, a prominent companion of the Imams, through the Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) direct guarantee of his salvation from Hellfire. The specific gesture of placing the hand on the chest underscores the sincerity and weight of this divine promise, reflecting the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Imams and the merit of their close companions. It serves as a key example of *al-kafala* (guarantee) in Shia tradition, linking personal piety with the Imam's authoritative word.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq guarantee for Ali ibn Yaqtin regarding the fire of Hell?

key_terms.أَلَّا تَمِسَّهُ النَّارُ: that the fire will not touch him
